question: As per Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, what was the percentage of waste processed in 2024-25, from 17.97% in 2015-16, indicating significant progress in waste management efficiency in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.807**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025**, monitors India's progress on environmental sustainability and waste management.
 
• In **2015-16**, the percentage of waste processed was **17.97%**, indicating the initial state of waste management efficiency in India.
 
• By **2024-25**, India showed significant progress with the percentage of waste processed increasing to **80.7%** (or 0.807 in decimal format).
 
• This improvement highlights India's advancements in implementing effective waste management practices, contributing towards meeting the targets of the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• The correct option **0.807** reflects the decimal representation of the waste processed percentage in 2024-25.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**

 
 
• The **SDGs**, established by the **United Nations in 2015**, consist of **17 goals** aimed at achieving a sustainable future for all by **2030**.
 
• Goal 12 of SDGs focuses on **responsible consumption and production**, including waste management and recycling.
 
• India actively monitors its progress through frameworks like the **National Indicator Framework**.
 
 
 
• **Waste Management in India:**
 
 
• India generates approximately **62 million tonnes of waste annually**, of which only **about 60%** is collected, and less than **50%** is processed.
 
• Efforts such as the **Swachh Bharat Mission** and policies on extended producer responsibility (EPR) have been implemented to improve waste processing rates.
 
• Technological advancements, public-private partnerships, and awareness campaigns play a critical role in enhancing waste management.
 
 
 
• **National Indicator Framework:**
 
 
• The **National Indicator Framework** is India's mechanism to track progress against the SDGs.
 
• It includes indicators specific to waste management, recycling, and sustainable urban development.
 
• The framework helps policymakers assess the effectiveness of programs and initiatives aimed at achieving sustainability targets.
 
 
 
• **Waste Processing Technologies:**
 
 
• Modern waste processing includes methods like **composting, recycling, waste-to-energy conversion, and landfill gas recovery.**
 
• India has been investing in **integrated waste management systems** to achieve higher efficiency in processing waste.
 
• Waste-to-energy plants convert non-recyclable waste into electricity, contributing to both waste reduction and energy generation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission:** Launched in **2014**, this initiative aims at achieving universal sanitation and a garbage-free India.
 
• **Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR):** Indian policies mandate producers to manage post-consumer waste, especially for plastics and electronics.
 
• **Waste-to-Energy (WTE):** India has set up several WTE plants to process municipal solid waste and generate energy.
 
• **Challenges:** Despite progress, challenges like informal recycling, lack of infrastructure, and low public awareness persist.
